newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe backs German chief on charge.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe backs German chief on charge.

text.p: CompuServe Corp said Wednesday it "vigorously" opposes an accusation filed against the chief of its German operation over the alleged distribution of child pornography through the online service.

German prosecutors said earlier they indicted the general manager of CompuServe's Munich-based unit, later identified by the company as Felix Somm, in connection with the distribution of child pornography, which is illegal in Germany.
In a statement, CompuServe said the formal accusation against Somm is "entirely groundless," adding that it believes he will ultimately be vindicated.
The company also said it will support Somm "through this personally trying period."
As reported earlier, the indictment was issued February 26, but was not made public until Wednesday in Germany.

The charges stemmed from an investigation launched in 1995, when German authorities forced CompuServe to shut down more than 200 Internet newsgroups through which individuals were suspected of transmitting child pornography.

CompuServe Wednesday reiterated it cannot control the content of Internet newsgroups, adding that it does not carry newsgroups that have been validly reported to the company as containing "child pornography and bestiality material."
CompuServe shares closed unchanged Wednesday at 11-3/8.
